title: Keep Your Hands Clean
summary: Maintain a flawless and positive public image by never being associated with mistakes or dirty work. Hide your blunders and achieve your goals indirectly by using scapegoats to take the blame and cat's paws to execute difficult or unsavory tasks on your behalf.
example: A Chinese ruler blamed a powerful man for his own military blunders to maintain control and avoid army resentment.
Cesare Borgia appointed a ruthless general to govern a lawless city, then had him executed in public to shift the blame for the harsh rule and gain the people's favor.
Cleopatra manipulated Julius Caesar and Mark Antony into doing her dirty work, securing her rule over Egypt without public backlash for killing her siblings.
A courtier acted as a cat's paw himself to elegantly help a friend clear his debt without making the favor obvious.
reversal: If your use of a cat's paw fails, your cover is blown, ruining your reputation and holding you accountable.
Occasionally, doing the dirty work yourself can be used to impose fear, though it should be done sparingly to avoid resentment.
Accepting a mistake directly can sometimes be used to show loyalty.
